newsitem.title: UK: Asian growth fuels Burmah Castrol profits.
newsitem.headline: Asian growth fuels Burmah Castrol profits.

text.p: Burmah Castrol, the British lubricants and chemicals firm, said on Monday it expected growth in Asia to continue after the region fuelled first-half profits.
Net attributable income motored 13 percent ahead to 67.7 million pounds ($105.4 million) with Castrol lubricant volumes climbing 10 percent in Asia -- double the rate of market growth.
The profit figure excludes a 23.2 million pound gain, stemming from the sale of fuels operations in Sweden, Turkey and Chile earlier this year.

Castrol held its profit level in Europe with a sharp fall in Germany offset by better results in Central and Eastern Europe. Castrol North America improved, although the consumer lubricants market showed no growth.
In Brazil, a new management team is making good progress in making the operations profitable, Burmah Castrom said.
The chemicals operations saw a seven percent increase in operating profit, pushed higher by strong growth at the screen printing ink division.
"We are confident that we can continue to deliver long term shareholder value by focusing on the organic developement of Castrol and chemicals," Burmah Castrol said in a statement. ($1=.6420 Pound)
